reference_action: Limp heirloom Christmas cactus after long dry period and old compacted soil. OP explicitly reports repotting a month earlier and looking better; central confirmed action is repot/refresh soil. Earlier watering and suggested patience/light are not independently confirmed as the recovery intervention.

sources.reason: Repot recommendation for limp old cactus directly matches what evaluated OP reports doing before improvement.
Explicit repot for old/root-filled medium and fresh airy soil recipe match replacement of old compacted medium; other water/rot suggestions not independently validated.
Repot is confined to soggy/rot branches of troubleshooting; described drought prompts soaking only, not confirmed old-soil replacement.

Explicit replacement of heavy compacted mix with airy soil retrieves the soil-refresh action. Partial only: wrong overwatering framing and additional trimming/drying/cinnamon are not validated by this case.
Fertilize, water when dry and patience, but no repot recommendation; water/feeding alone is not the reported intervention.

resolved.reason: Over/underwatering remain unresolved possibilities but repot is the main recommendation and matches outcome; propagation alternative is unspecified and unvalidated.

harmfulness.reason: “Check the roots” is a reasonable preliminary safeguard. “Or chop n prop” offers unnecessary cutting without explaining when it is warranted, though the main repot action matches the observed recovery.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “I repotted mine ... it got a lot better” supplies the confirmed action. No explanation of old compacted soil or handling of the already-watered rootball distinguishes this case from the comment’s competing over/underwatering possibilities.

feasibility.reason: Root checking and repotting are familiar tasks. The answer supplies no substrate, pot-size or propagation method, so “Re pot it Or chop n prop” leaves substantial implementation choices to the reader.
